rationale: Sources 3 (Medscape) and 4 (Empathia) independently address renal tubular sodium handling reducing lithium clearance with thiazides and acute neurological lithium toxicity symptoms, whereas Source 1 only notes in general summary text that diuretics and NSAIDs alter renal function without explaining mechanisms or toxicity symptoms, and Source 2 is blocked by a ResearchGate security check.

Only Source 1 (HHS.gov) substantively states the 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart D requirement to notify the HHS Secretary when a breach of unsecured PHI affects 500 or more individuals; Source 3 (eCFR) contains only a verbatim statutory sentence on media notification already duplicated in Source 1 (and verbatim statutory reprints count as 1), Source 2 omits the 500-individual threshold and deadline, and Source 4 is an off-topic FTC 404 page.

Four independent domains (Sources 1-4, capped at 3) consistently explain that strawberries are botanically aggregate accessory fruits rather than true berries because their flesh develops from accessory receptacle tissue bearing multiple ovaries/achenes; hazard_tier is medium because botanical morphology and taxonomy are scientific facts without immediate safety or liability risk.

Source 1 (Food Safety Institute) explains Bacillus cereus spore survival, room-temperature germination in cooked rice, and rapid-onset emetic cereulide production, and Source 3 (PMC) confirms cereulide's extreme thermal/processing stability, whereas Source 2 returned a ScienceDirect error page and Source 4 (Cleveland Clinic) gives only a general patient overview omitting spore germination, cereulide, and heat stability.
